target_customer: Employers and employees buying individual health insurance through an HRA stipend
problem: Employees wanted to choose their own health insurance, and employers wanted to give a tax-free stipend instead of running a group plan, but the tools to administer it were missing.
business_model: B2B software and payments for health reimbursement arrangements, plus brokerage
product_category: Health benefits fintech, ICHRA and HRA administration

founders.name: Kevin Cox
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led engineering teams at Clipboard Health. Later founded Adaptional.

founders.name: Suril Kantaria
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Primer and xAI; the xAI role may postdate Savvy.

exit.reason: Take Command says it acquired Savvy's HRA technology and intellectual property; terms not disclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed payment cards, reimbursement flows and insurance data across 50 state markets, which is standard fintech work with a regulatory layer.

defensibility.rationale: Insurance licensing and state coverage helped, but the YC page and press show no data or network moat, and the buyer took the technology rather than the whole company.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Take Command, the HRA incumbent, acquired Savvy's HRA technology in June 2022.

market_need_then: New ICHRA regulation took effect in 2020, and the YC page says Savvy was one of the first to market after it and scaled to tens of millions of dollars in volume.

branding.domain_note: Operated at gosavvy.com, which redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page as of this research.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly real word, but no press or community material about the brand was found, and the exact .com was not owned.

outcome_analysis: Savvy rode the 2020 ICHRA regulation and reached tens of millions of dollars in volume across all 50 state markets, according to its YC profile. In June 2022 incumbent Take Command bought its HRA technology and intellectual property, which Take Command's own announcement frames as a technology purchase rather than a full company deal. Funding is only partly known, and price was not disclosed, so how strong the outcome was cannot be judged.
notes: A seed round dated March 2020 and a total of about 2.3 million dollars appear only in aggregator snippets (Seedtable, Coverager listing, Village) with no investor names, so they are unverified and not recorded as a round. YC page names Marc Andreessen and the founders of One Medical and Indeed as backers without a round. Competitor search returned only current comparison pages, so the list is empty. Founder education not found. CB Insights and others call it a company acquisition while Take Command says technology and IP. Completeness pass: the March 2020 seed is now recorded from Seedtable (no amount given there; investors as reported by Seedtable, while CB Insights lists Y Combinator, Alumni Ventures, Giant Ventures and Take Command Health) and rests on a single database. The roughly 2.3M total and CB Insights total of 150K conflict and are not recorded; the amount is null.
